title: ZABEL – Learning better dental health: Feasibility study on low-threshold dental care for primary school children using digital technologies
summary:
Healthy teeth are particularly important for children, as they can prevent pain, sleep problems and problems at school. Children with tooth decay are more likely to miss school and have a lower overall quality of life than children with healthy teeth. Children from disadvantaged backgrounds are particularly affected by this. Good dental health can give them better opportunities for their future development.

In this study, first-grade children aged 6 to 7 years at selected schools in Kiel will be examined. The dental examinations will take place once a year and will be repeated until the end of primary school. In addition, the study will examine how well children understand their own dental condition. It will compare whether an explanation using only words or an explanation with additional images from a digital dental scan is easier for children to understand. The study will also record the children's well-being in relation to oral health and their previous experiences with visits to the dentist.
It is assumed that a purely verbal explanation of dental health has no advantage over an explanation with additional visual aids.
conditions: Investigation of the understanding of dental findings with and without the use of intraoral scans

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The inclusion criteria are sufficient cooperation and sufficient mouth opening of the child to perform a scan. No acute dental or general medical complaints.
As well as the present study consent and a subject information sheet signed by the legal guardians.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for participation in the study are existing general illnesses (such as HIV, hepatitis, epilepsy) and insufficient adherence on the part of the child, as well as the absence of consent from the child and/or legal guardian.
